maria: drafting an RFC appendix for splitting large runtime services into narrow capability modules. short sanity check? trying to capture acceptance criteria, risks, and staged migration options.

aj: love the idea. can you paste the appendix here so we can comment inline?

maria: pasted below — it's intentionally prescriptive so owners have a clear checklist. open to calls outs.

```
RFC APPENDIX: MODULE EXTRACTION RUNBOOK
- scope: each module implements a single business capability and owns its minimal data and side effects
- contract: explicit protobuf/http spec with version header; any breaking change requires two-phase deprecation
- compatibility window: new contract must accept old-version header for at least 3 deploy cycles
- gating: feature-flag + tenant-scoped rollout; default OFF for existing tenants
- data migration: prefer read-through shadow + asynchronous backfill; if dual-write chosen, require monotonic write-id and at-least-once dedupe strategy
- stateful caches: provide prefix namespace mapping + tombstone semantics; include a compact/repair job and migration TTL
- idempotency: all write adapters must be idempotent and support retry-without-side-effects
- perf budget: adapter latency < 10ms p50 and < 50ms p95; adapter CPU/alloc must be declared
- ops controls: circuit-breaker + throttling knobs per-tenant; emergency kill-switch to re-route to legacy path
- observability: per-module traces, span naming conventions, request tags (tenant, module, version), and billing meters (tokens, ops-seconds)
- tests: unit + contract tests; integration harness (golden-traffic) that replays recorded production traces against the new module; chaos/latency injection smoke test
- rollout plan: dev -> staging(golden-traffic) -> tenant-canary(by tenant id ranges) -> ramp percent -> full-cutover
- validation gates: error-rate delta < 0.5% absolute and latency delta within declared perf budget for 72h at each ramp step
- rollback: automated routing change to legacy path within 60s + database safepoint for point-in-time rollback
- cost guardrails: predicted billing delta and a hard budget throttle to prevent runaway spend; alerting on cost-per-token spikes
- deprecation/cleanup: require a tech-debt ticket with owner and an explicit cleanup date no later than 6 months after cutover
```

taylor: strong. two suggestions: 1) include a schema-version header on all persisted records so consumers can detect shape mismatches; 2) define a tiny adapter pattern in the codebase (example impl) so teams don't invent incompatible shims.

sam: ops additions: require a synthetic "canary probe" that runs every 60s against the new module for the first week and 5m for the next 3 weeks. also add dashboard panels for token-rate, p95 latency, error-rate, and CPU/gpu-util mapped to module tag.

aj: migration strategy question: for splitting a KV-backed feature, do we prefer namespace remapping with proxy-translation or copy-on-read?

maria: options and tradeoffs:
- proxy-translation: single source of truth, fast cutover, but proxy becomes critical path and needs tight perf SLAs
- copy-on-read (lazy copy): low proxy load, slower validation, can expose new module to cold-cache hit patterns
- bulk-copy with switch: fastest validation but requires strong backfill tooling and space for duplicate data

maria: my bias: start with proxy-translation in small tenant canaries to validate semantics, then schedule background bulk-copy for long-term efficiency.

aj: agree. if we proxy, we need a per-tenant throttle and a runaway protection that can flip to sampling mode (1%). add that to the runbook.

sam: also add a verification job that scans a sample of keys across tenant ranges daily for 7 days, reporting divergence rate. threshold for concern: >0.1% mismatches.

infra-bot: deploy-bot posted: patch/rfc-appendix 2234567920 by @maria  staging applied :white_check_mark:

maria: action items for owners before merge:
- author example adapter in runtime repo (link-to-pr placeholder)
- fill migration checklist template in docs with explicit fallback steps
- schedule runbook dry-run with eng-oncall and sres (30-60m)
- add synthetic canary probes and cost panels in staging org
- assign rollback owner and emergency page for 72h after cutover

taylor: i can draft the adapter example and perf microbenchmarks. i'll also add the schema-version header enforcement in the serializer lib.

aj: i'll review the migration checklist and volunteer to run the first dry-run for the KV split.

sam: i'll prepare the dashboard widgets and the daily divergence job template.

maria: thanks. i'll fold these into the RFC appendix and open a docs PR. planning to land EOD unless new objections.

aj: no objections. go ahead. :+1:

taylor: looks good to me. :rocket:

sam: all set.

maria: merging into RFC branch and will ping when PR is up. thanks everyone.
